intent: Review and fix adapter-scoped Wi-Fi management before the first mainline commit.
execution: Sequential review in the main thread, as required by the user's AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Bind every SecretAgent password request to a verified adapter
findings.why_it_matters: An ambiguous or unmapped profile request opened a generic password prompt without deviceId. The prompt escaped adapter removal handling, and profile ownership was not checked again after password input.
evidence: The original ambiguous-profile regression expected a password prompt without deviceId.
Five targeted regression cases failed before the fix: ambiguous ownership, absent ownership, unreadable ownership, unmapped single-device ownership and ownership changes during password input.
A uniquely activating connection now identifies its adapter even when the same multi-connect profile is already active on another adapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the live adapter before and after input, prefer the only activating device, and reject requests whose adapter cannot be determined.

findings.title: Cancel only the matching profile's SecretAgent prompt
findings.why_it_matters: CancelGetSecrets cancelled all prompts for an adapter. A delayed cancellation from an old profile could dismiss a newer network password on that same adapter.
evidence: The cancellation regression failed because the unrelated manual password task was already done after CancelGetSecrets.
SecretAgent prompts are now grouped by profile, while separate token-to-device metadata supports adapter removal.
The removal regression confirms the removed adapter's profile prompt is cancelled while the other adapter's prompt remains pending.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate profile cancellation from device cancellation using independent prompt group and device metadata.

findings.title: Exclude hotspot and peer profiles from client connections
findings.why_it_matters: A compatible Wi-Fi profile can use AP, Ad-hoc or Mesh mode. Matching only SSID and security could activate such a profile when the user intended to join a scanned network.
evidence: All three mode regression cases activated the existing non-infrastructure profile before the fix.
Filtering saved client profiles to infrastructure mode now causes the scanned network flow to create its own infrastructure connection.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter non-infrastructure modes from saved client profiles before listing or reusing them.

residual_risks: Physical connection, disconnection, USB unplug/replug and hardware button acceptance remain recorded in docs/udeck/multi-wifi-2026-11-06.md.
testing_gaps: The SSH connection uses the USB adapter, so destructive network changes and physical unplugging require onsite acceptance.
